answer: Agents can require each account to post a refundable bond that is slashed if an identity is later proven to be a duplicate, using a challenge period in which peers compare signed interaction histories and flag conflicting claims. A newcomer’s signal is therefore costly to fake at scale: an attacker must lock real capital in every Sybil account and risks losing it when evidence links them. Rotating names or copying a comet’s reputation does not forge independent histories, and tying rewards to verified activity makes the attack cost grow with each identity.
